title: Crisis to Celebration | Rela Hospital
department: Neurosciences
content:
Master Dishyadev met with an accident on October 27, 2023 when he was riding pillion on his mother’s scooter. He fell down from the vehicle when it skidded on the wet road and became unconscious. His fall caused fragments to impinge his brain.

He was rushed to Rela Hospital, where Dr M. Anbuselvam, Senior Consultant, Institute of Neuroscience, Neurosurgery, and his team conducted an emergency operation. Post that, he regained his consciousness, stayed in the ICU for 3 days and was finally, discharged in a week. He has returned to normalcy and has recovered completely and his father thanks Rela Hospital for the same.

title: Resilient Heart | Rela Hospital
department: Department of Cardiology
content:
Ms. Priya Angamuthu, a nursing student from Salem had been facing a heart condition since 2020, wherein she had symptoms such as weakness in hands and legs and inability to walk. Despite undergoing treatment for one and half years, nothing worked for her.

On consultation with a cardiologist, she was prescribed medicines, which were futile. Things became worse and she finally consulted Dr. V. Narendra Kumar, Senior Consultant- Interventional Cardiology, Advanced Heart Failure and Transplant Cardiology,from Rela Hospital.

She received medications that not only kept her active but also paved the way for a successful heart transplant. She has fully recovered and is regaining normalcy, the ability to breathe effortlessly, and the freedom to walk without hindrance. She has resumed her studies and is in good health.

title: Walking into Wellness | Rela Hospital
content:
Mr. Yuvaraj from Mayiladuthurai was worried when he noticed swelling in his legs without a clear cause. As it persisted, he observed water oozing from the affected area, leading to an infection that severely impacted his ability to urinate and eat. At the suggestion of a friend, he got himself promptly admitted to Rela Hospital.

Reflecting on his experience, he highlights how Prof. Mohamed Rela, Chairman & Director, Rela Hospital, meticulously explained the necessary steps for his operation. He is grateful to the hospital for restoring his ability to walk and for ensuring his return home in good condition.

title: Resilient Strides
department: Orthopaedics
content:
In 2009, Mr. Umapathy from Chromepet experienced a fall while getting down from a bus. He had successfully undergone a hip replacement for a left hip joint fracture and had healed well. Recently, the pain had become intolerable despite medication, prompting admission for further evaluation. Seeking consultation with Dr. Ashok S. Gavaskar, Clinical Lead in Orthopaedics, he reported a vague pain in his left hip.

Subsequent ultrasound scans revealed an infection in his hip joint, leading to a crucial 6-hour surgery. Following recovery from the infection, Mr. Umapathy underwent a re-operation a month later. Today, he is free from pain and infection, experiencing excellent functionality in his hips. He is grateful for the successful outcome and expresses his sincere thanks to Dr. Ashok S. Gavaskar for restoring his ability to walk normally.

title: Baby Arhaar’s battle with tyrosinemia
department: Paediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Transplantation, Advanced Paediatrics
content:
Baby Arheer from Punjab was battling with a rare liver disease, tyrosinemia type 1 when she was 6 months old. She started losing weight and did not begin teething even after 6 months. Her mother took her to the local hospital for treatment where she was diagnosed with Liver Cirrhosis and Multifocal Carcinoma in her liver and she was also told that she may not survive more than four days. The only solution suggested was liver transplantation and the chances of survival were only 40%. Her mother was worried and was left with no hope.

She met Dr. Jagadeesh Menon VR, Consultant, Pediatric Hepatology when he visited Chandigarh who gave her the hope that the child’s life can be saved with a liver transplantation. She visited Rela Hospital, Chennai to meet Prof. Mohamed Rela, Chairman & Director of Rela Hospital. After a thorough diagnosis, the procedures for liver transplantation were initiated and the mother came forward to be the donor.

After a successful liver transplantation, the child started getting healthier. She gained weight, started teething, and became more active and joyful post-surgery. The mother expresses her gratitude to Prof. Mohamed Rela, Dr. Jagadeesh Menon VR, and their expert team of doctors who saved her child’s life.

This story highlights the significance of compassionate and dedicated doctors striving to provide their patients with the best of care.

We wish Arheer the best of health.

title: 27 yeard old Kuwait man’s triumph through liver transplantation

title: Triumphing over Deep Vein Thrombosis. | Dr. Paraneetharan Marimuthu
department: Internal Medicine, Neurosciences, Department Of Neuro Spine, Neurosurgery
content:
Triumphing over Deep Vein Thrombosis..

62 year old Tamilarasi from Karaikudi lost functions in both of her legs for the past 10 months. Her normal life was affected because of the same. Her son, Nagarajan explains how he had tried at multiple hospitals and with multiple treatment options despite which his mother was bedridden.

They visited Rela Hospital, Chennai through a family reference and consulted with Dr. J. Prabhakaran, Senior Consultant, Internal Medicine and Diabetology, who then directed them to Dr. Paraneetharan Marimuthu, Senior Consultant and Clinical Lead, Neuroscience, Neuro Spine, Neurosurgery.

After tests and MRI scan, she was diagnosed with Deep Vein Thrombosis and surgery was the only suggested option of recovery. It was a successful surgery and Tamilarasi got back to her normal life in just 2-3 days after surgery.

Nagarajan explains how his mother is able to walk again and do her activities on her own. He expresses his gratitude to Dr. Paraneetharan Marimuthu, Senior Consultant and Clinical Lead, Neuroscience, Neuro Spine, Neurosurgery and the hospital management for helping his mother get back on her foot again.

Stories like this motivate us to provide our patient community with the best of care.

title: To a story of hope and healing | Dr (BRIG) K Shanmuganandan
content:
To a story of hope and healing..

Yesuraj, a middle aged IT professional, from Thanjavur has been battling chronic Rheumatoid Arthritis for many years.

He has been fighting with inflammatory back ache for 10 years and was treated with various forms of medicine including self medicating himself with painkillers which resulted in kidney damage.

He went through a general checkup past month to find a protein leak in urine and rise of urea creatinine in blood. Fortunately, he consulted with Dr. B. Karthikeyan, Senior Consultant, Nephrology, who suggested to meet Dr (BRIG) K Shanmuganandan, Rheumatologist, Rela Hospital.

Post tests, he was diagnosed with Ankylosing Spondylitis along with NSI induced nephropathy. He was put on anti TNF biological called Adalimumab twice a month which gave him a good relief.

Yesuraj explains that he feels much better, healthy and relaxed post two sittings. He expresses his gratitude to the hospital management and Dr (BRIG) K Shanmuganandan, for his timely treatment and thanks the doctor for making him do his daily activities without help.

Stories like this motivate us to provide our patient community with the best of care.

title: A Sri Lankan’s tale of overcoming a life threatening brain tumor | Dr. M. Anbuselvam
department: Neurosciences, Neurosurgery
content:
A Sri Lankan’s tale of overcoming a life threatening brain tumor.

38 year old, Noorul Haseena from Atulugama, Sri Lanka, developed a headache and started losing her vision gradually. Upon visiting the doctor and through CT and MRI scan, they found out that she had a tumor in her brain. The women got into alternative sources of treatment, until the headache got worse leading to vomiting and loss of vision.

She was then referred to Rela Hospital, where she consulted with Dr M. Anbuselvam, Senior Consultant, Neuroscience and Neurosurgery. The doctor repeated the MRI scan to find out a large lesion in her frontal lobe of the brain. Post diagnosis, it proved to be a tuberculous lesion and she was suggested with further medical treatment.

Noorul Haseena was discharged in three days with medications to follow for one year. Her husband explains how she is back to normal and expresses his gratitude to the expert team of doctors and the hospital management for treating his wife.

This story highlights the significance of seeking appropriate medical attention at the right time. It also emphasizes the importance of compassionate and dedicated doctors striving to provide their patients with the best care.

title: Testimonial by Vebbin | Dr Sunil | Rela Hospital
department: Orthopaedics
content: Vebbin, a 14-year-old boy from Tambaram, met with an unfortunate accident as he fell from the terrace while playing with his pets. He sustained multiple fractures in both lower limbs and lost a lot of blood, and was sent into a state of shock. Looking at his severe state, he was immediately taken to Rela Hospital. Some of his injuries required expert care to put his joints in working condition. Dr. Ashok S. Gavaskar, Clinical Lead – Orthopaedics, Head – Joint Replacement Services, Arthroplasty (Joint Replacement), Orthopaedics, attended him. He was in ICU for two days because of his life-threatening condition, post which he was stabilised. The initial surgery got over in the injured spinal cord and thigh. Unfortunately, he had a major fracture in the leg, for which they had a plate. He was admitted for two weeks. Despite his pain, he was motivated that just 12 weeks after a painful surgery, he was back to his routine. He was then asked to walk with support for six weeks. After resuscitation, spanning days, we were finally able to save his life. We wish him the best in his life and future endeavours.

title: Captain Mohammad Zahir-Ul-Islam-Khan’s Testimonial
department: Liver Disease & Transplantation
content:
Group Captain Mohammad Zahir-Ul-Islam-Khan, actively serving at the Bangladesh Air Force, was rushed to Rela Hospital on the 15th of July owing to complaints of severe illness and jaundice. His bilirubin serum had shot up to 38 by then. His Director General of Medical Service recommended Rela Institute to him, and he was immediately brought within the next three hours from Bangladesh.

He was received by the people of Rela Hospital from the airport with their ambulance. For over another month, he went through many procedures, operations, and treatments, under the direct supervision of Prof. Mohamed Rela. Group Captain also states that because of Prof. Mohamed Rela, he can sit straight now and talk in good condition.

On the whole, he states the three critical aspects of the institution which he felt were the reasons for him to recover soon from the complications he was facing. Starting with specialised doctors who are always keen on helping you, good supporting staff who make you feel at home through your time of stay there, and lastly, the infrastructure that makes them the best in the business.

It is testimonials like this that help us in building a better environment for the future of healthcare services and serve as many people as possible.

title: India’s Youngest Successful Liver Transplantation on a One-Month-Old Baby, performed at Dr Rela Hospital
department: Liver Disease & Transplantation, Paediatric HPB Surgery & Liver Transplantation
content:
India’s Youngest Successful Liver Transplantation on a One-Month-Old Baby, performed at Dr Rela Hospital
 
~10 Hours of Marathon Surgery at Dr. Rela Hospital gives a new ray of hope to a one-month-old baby’s parents ~
 

Dr. Rela Hospital performed India’s first successful liver transplantation on a one-month-old baby on 23rd July in the city. The youngest child to undergo liver transplantation in the country is now doing well and is under the hospital’s postoperative care.

This rare surgery was performed on Aadav (name changed) from Mumbai, who had developed vomiting in the first week of birth, requiring immediate hospitalization. What was believed to be a simple infection, was later diagnosed as urea cycle disorder, which is a metabolic disorder.

When the parents realized that liver transplantation was the only curative treatment option, they shifted the child from Mumbai to Dr. Rela Hospital. The 10-hour long surgery was performed by an expert team of pediatric transplant surgeons and pediatric anesthetists.

Commenting on the first of its kind surgery, Prof Mohamed Rela, Chairman and Managing Director of Dr Rela Hospital, said, “I am glad that a quick diagnosis and timely supportive measures were initiated in mumbai that has prevented the child from having brain damage. The parents took the right decision to let their baby undergo liver transplantation. No centre in India has so far performed liver transplantation on such a young infant.

He added that though metabolic disorders are rare, they are important causes of liver diseases and liver failures in newborns. However, liver transplantation can save them effectively. Though technically difficult neither the weight, nor the age of the baby is a limiting factor.

Talking about the disorder, Dr Naresh Shanmugam, Paediatric Hepatologist and Director for Women & Child Health Department at Dr Rela Hospital, said, “Urea cycle disorder results in high ammonia levels in the blood. The condition refers to the inability of the liver to convert ammonia, which is produced as a byproduct while the body metabolis es proteins, into urea. As the presence of ammonia in the blood increases, it causes swelling in the brain resulting in coma and even death. Immediate action includes stopping protein intake and do dialysis to remove the ammonia. But liver transplantation is the permanent solution.

He added that on average one in 3000 children are born with some form of metabolic disorders in the world. The metabolic disorders can be effectively detected by what is known as the heel prick test, which requires only one drop of blood.

Dr.Ilankumaran Kaliamoorthy, Chairman, Medical Advisory Board at Dr Rela Hospital, said, “Performing liver transplantation in newborn & underweight babies is very challenging. At Dr. Rela Institute, we believe that with our expertise, world-class facilities & infrastructure, age is no barrier for liver transplantation. We have emerged as the largest liver transplant unit performing liver transplantation for a wide age range from newborns to over 70 years old.

Dr. Rela Hospital have the expertise and well-equipped paediatric and newborn intensive care unit to perform complex liver, bone marrow, kidney and intestinal transplant surgeries on babies successfully.
